title: Oops Reversal
teaches: The Oops as we trade it: one daily candle in a leader after an orderly pullback, that opens under the prior close, trades under the prior day's low and closes back over the prior close, with a Super Oops closing over the prior high; the buy is a market order as price trades back over the prior close after the undercut, the stop sits a few cents under the Oops day's low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, a close back under the prior close is a warning and the stop is the exit.

questions.q: The main Oops day opens under the prior close, trades under the prior low and closes over the prior close.
questions.why: True. Those are the three tests of the main Oops day: the open, the undercut and the close back over.
questions.lesson_line: Open under, undercut, close back over: that is the Oops.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The Oops day opens under the prior close and closes back over the prior ___.
questions.why: Close. The Oops day closes back over the prior close. If it never reclaims, it is not an Oops.
questions.lesson_line: The Oops day must end back over the prior close.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The Oops day trades under the prior day's ___ and then closes back over the prior close.
questions.why: Low. The Oops day trades under the prior day's low before it reclaims the close. That undercut is the trap.
questions.lesson_line: The undercut of the prior low is the trap.

questions.q: What makes an Oops a Super Oops?
choices: It closes over the prior high
It trades over the prior high
It opens over the prior close
It gaps up on news
questions.answer: It closes over the prior high
questions.why: It closes over the prior high. The whole prior day is engulfed. A Super Oops is any Oops that does that.
questions.lesson_line: Close over the prior high, and the Oops is a Super.

wrong.It trades over the prior high: The Super Oops is a close over the prior high, not a trade over it.
wrong.It opens over the prior close: The Oops opens under the prior close.
wrong.It gaps up on news: An Oops opens under the prior close, and news-sized days are a mistake.

questions.q: Williams' original Oops opens under the prior day's low.
questions.why: True. Radge, Unger and Deepvue all read Williams that way. Our main version only needs an open under the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Williams opens under the low. Our main version opens under the close.

questions.q: Where does the Oops stop go?
choices: A few cents under the Oops-day low
A few cents under the prior day's low
A few cents under the prior close
A few cents under the 200-day
questions.answer: A few cents under the Oops-day low
questions.why: A few cents under the Oops day's low, the point where the trap was set.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the low the trap was set at.

wrong.A few cents under the prior day's low: The Oops day trades under it. A stop even a few cents below sits inside the trap.
wrong.A few cents under the prior close: The prior close is the buy point, not the stop.
wrong.A few cents under the 200-day: The 200-day is context. The stop sits under the Oops-day low.

questions.q: In a Red market the Oops, like every long setup, is mostly cash.
questions.why: True. Green or Yellow, and Orange only for an A+ Oops. In a Red market it is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first. Red means cash.

questions.q: In our scans, when does the Oops buy fill?
choices: As it trades back over the close
As soon as it opens under the close
At the open, before the undercut
At the next day's open
questions.answer: As it trades back over the close
questions.why: In our scans it fills as price trades back over the prior close, once the day has traded under the prior low. No reclaim, no trade.
questions.lesson_line: Undercut first, then the reclaim of the close. That is our scans' buy.

wrong.As soon as it opens under the close: An open under the close is only the first test. The undercut and the reclaim must follow.
wrong.At the open, before the undercut: A buy at the open can fill before the undercut.
wrong.At the next day's open: Our scans buy on the Oops day itself, not at the next open.

questions.q: The Oops buy is a resting buy-stop placed at the open.
questions.why: False. A resting buy-stop at the open can fill before the undercut. Use a market order when the trigger prints.
questions.lesson_line: Alert at the prior close, then a market order. No resting stop at the open.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The prior close sits ___% to 12% below the 20-day high.
questions.why: 3%. The prior close should be 3% to 12% under the 20-day high. Less than that is a dip at the highs.
questions.lesson_line: A real pullback first: 3% to 12% off the 20-day high.

questions.q: An Oops can fire on a dip of under 1% from the 20-day high.
questions.why: False. A real pullback comes first, 3% to 12% off the 20-day high. A dip at the highs has nothing to reverse from.
questions.lesson_line: No pullback, nothing to reverse.

questions.q: Where should the Oops-day low tag?
choices: A 21- or 50-day, or a clear level
Open air well above the old highs
A brand new 52-week high today
Nothing in particular; any spot

questions.why: The 21-day EMA or 50-day SMA, or a visible level such as a flag low or a gap. Location matters.
questions.lesson_line: The undercut should tag something the market can see.

wrong.Open air well above the old highs: There is no level there to undercut.
wrong.A brand new 52-week high today: An Oops follows a pullback, not a new high.
wrong.Nothing in particular; any spot: Location matters. The low should tag a level.

questions.q: The Oops needs a red prior day.
questions.why: False. A red prior day is preferred, not required.
questions.lesson_line: Red prior day: preferred. Not required.

questions.why: False. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. A stop with the broker is an appointment.

questions.q: What floor must an Oops stock clear?
choices: $10 and $20 million a day
$5 and $5 million a day
$2 and $10,000 a day
No floor for a clean leader
questions.why: $10 a share and $20 million a day. Thin stocks are not even watched.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars a share, twenty million a day. Below that, no Oops.

wrong.$5 and $5 million a day: Too low. Our floor is $10 a share and $20 million a day.
wrong.$2 and $10,000 a day: Far under our floor of $10 and $20 million.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Never buy an Oops more than ___% above the prior close.
questions.why: 4%. A buy more than 4% above the prior close is a chase. The stop would be too far away.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the prior close and I am done.

questions.q: Why does the stop sit under the Oops-day low?
choices: It marks where the trap was set
It is the middle of the range
It equals the app's first target
It is where volume peaked
questions.answer: It marks where the trap was set
questions.why: It is the point where the trap was set. If price trades below it, the trap failed.
questions.lesson_line: Under the Oops-day low the trap has failed. That is the exit.

wrong.It is the middle of the range: The stop is not a midpoint. It is the low of the trap.
wrong.It equals the app's first target: Targets are 3R and 5R thirds, not stops.
wrong.It is where volume peaked: Volume is not part of the Oops.

questions.q: A Super Oops only needs the day's high to pass the prior high.
questions.why: False. A Super Oops is a close over the prior high, not just a trade over it.
questions.lesson_line: The Super is a close over the prior high.

questions.q: The 20-day high is 100.00 and the prior close is 91.50. How far has it pulled back, in percent?
questions.why: 8.5%. That is inside the 3% to 12% range, a real pullback to reverse from.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the pullback from the 20-day high. Inside 3% to 12%.

questions.q: Filled at 31.51 with the stop at 31.12. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 1.24%. Well inside 3%, so the stop is honest. This is the ACN trade.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop. A close stop is what the Oops gives you.

questions.q: Is it an Oops day?
choices: Yes, it passes all three tests
No, it never opened under the prior low
No, it did not close over the prior high
No, the undercut was too shallow
questions.story: Yesterday: high 50.60, low 49.40, close 50.00. Today: open 49.70, low 49.10, close 50.30.
questions.answer: Yes, it passes all three tests
questions.why: Yes. It opened under the prior close, traded under the prior low and closed over the prior close. It is the main version.
questions.lesson_line: Check the three tests one by one against yesterday.

wrong.No, it never opened under the prior low: That is Williams' stricter version. The main version needs an open under the prior close.
wrong.No, it did not close over the prior high: Over the prior high makes it a Super Oops, a quality mark.
wrong.No, the undercut was too shallow: Any trade under the prior low counts as the undercut.

questions.q: What do you call it?
choices: A Super Oops
A Williams Oops
A plain Oops, nothing more
A Kicker
questions.story: Yesterday: high 50.60, low 49.40, close 50.00. Today opens at 49.70, trades down to 49.10 and closes at 50.80.
questions.why: A Super Oops. It closed at 50.80, over the prior high of 50.60. It opened at 49.70, over the prior low, so it is not a Williams open.
questions.lesson_line: Close over the prior high makes it a Super.

wrong.A Williams Oops: It opened at 49.70, over the prior low of 49.40. Williams opens under the prior low.
wrong.A plain Oops, nothing more: It closed over the prior high, which makes it a Super.
wrong.A Kicker: A Kicker gaps up over a red day. This opened under the prior close.

questions.q: In our scans, which touch of the prior close fills the buy?
choices: The 11:00 one, after the undercut
The 9:40 touch of the prior close
Either one; both touched 50.00
Neither; wait for the daily close
questions.story: The prior close is 50.00 and the prior low 49.40. The stock opens under 50.00, touches it at 9:40, then breaks 49.40. At 11:00 it is back at 50.00.
questions.why: The 11:00 touch, after the undercut. Buying the touch of the prior close before the undercut is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Undercut first. A touch before it is not the trigger.

wrong.The 9:40 touch of the prior close: That touch came before the undercut. A touch of the prior close before the undercut is not a trigger.
wrong.Either one; both touched 50.00: Only the touch after the undercut counts.
wrong.Neither; wait for the daily close: Our scans buy during the day, as a market order when the trigger prints.

questions.q: Do you buy it now?
choices: No, over 4% above the prior close
Yes, a strong Oops often continues
Yes, with a smaller stop to fit
Yes, at half size to stay safe
questions.story: The prior close is 50.00. You missed the reclaim. At 11:30 the stock is at 52.30.
questions.answer: No, over 4% above the prior close
questions.why: No. 52.30 is more than 4% above the prior close of 50.00. Never chase; the stop stays put and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the prior close, you missed it. Let it go.

wrong.Yes, a strong Oops often continues: Strength is not a reason to chase.
wrong.Yes, with a smaller stop to fit: You do not tighten the stop to fit.
wrong.Yes, at half size to stay safe: Half size does not change the rule.

questions.q: Do you buy it?
choices: No, a report is inside 3 days
Yes, it is an Oops, not earnings
Yes, at half size
Yes, then sell before the report
questions.story: A clean Oops reclaims the prior close. The company reports earnings in two days.
questions.answer: No, a report is inside 3 days
questions.why: No. No new Oops buy in the 3 days before a report. A report this close can gap the stock past your stop.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.Yes, it is an Oops, not earnings: The report window is its own rule.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change the rule.
wrong.Yes, then sell before the report: The rule is no new buys inside the window.

questions.q: A random big red bar came three days before. What does it do to the Oops?
choices: It removes it from the list
Nothing, it is old history now
It upgrades it to a Super Oops
It adds a point to the grade
questions.answer: It removes it from the list
questions.why: It takes the stock off the list. The pullback should be orderly, with no bar in the 5 sessions before that drops over 4%.
questions.lesson_line: An orderly drift only. A big red bar in the days before is out.

wrong.Nothing, it is old history now: A big red bar in the days before is a named mistake to buy.
wrong.It upgrades it to a Super Oops: A Super Oops is a close over the prior high.
wrong.It adds a point to the grade: It takes grade away. The stock comes off the list.

questions.q: Your move at the close?
choices: Hold to the stop; do not add
Sell at the close, it failed
Add a second lot on the dip
Move the stop under 31.30
questions.story: You bought the reclaim of the 31.50 prior close at 31.52, the way our scans do, with the stop at 31.12. The day closes at 31.30, back under the prior close, above your stop.
questions.answer: Hold to the stop; do not add
questions.why: Hold to the stop and do not add. The day closed back under the prior close, so the trade is wrong as an Oops. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A close back under the prior close is a warning. The stop does the rest.

wrong.Sell at the close, it failed: The stop is the exit, not a weak close.
wrong.Add a second lot on the dip: We never add after a warning.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Nothing; the stop is the plan
Wish you had used a wider stop
Buy back at once
Move the stop lower next time
questions.story: You bought at 67.48 with the stop at 66.70. The next day it opens at 68.48, then sells straight through your stop to 66.63.
questions.answer: Nothing; the stop is the plan
questions.why: Nothing. A perfect-looking day gives no warning, and the stop is the whole plan. This was ADBE on 2014-03-12.
questions.lesson_line: A perfect-looking Oops gives no warning. The stop is the plan.

wrong.Wish you had used a wider stop: A wider stop is a bigger loss. The stop did its job.
wrong.Buy back at once: Buy again only on a new trigger.
wrong.Move the stop lower next time: A stop never moves down or wider.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
choices: 30.85, the first 30-minute low
31.12, the original stop price
Out at once; the loss is past 2R
The open, 30.95, the gap price
questions.story: You bought at 31.52 with the stop at 31.12. The next morning it gaps open at 30.95. The first 30-minute low is 30.85.
questions.why: 30.85. A gap down through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.31.12, the original stop price: The stop is already through. The 30-minute low is the new stop.
wrong.Out at once; the loss is past 2R: The loss at the 30-minute low is inside the 2R ceiling.
wrong.The open, 30.95, the gap price: The open is not the decision. The 30-minute low is.

questions.q: What is the plan at 3R?
choices: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
Sell it all and lock in the 3R
Sell half, leave the stop alone
Hold all, nudge the stop up
questions.story: You bought at 149.22 with the stop at 146.52. The Oops reaches 3R.
questions.answer: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third and move the stop to breakeven. The first trim is a third at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: At 3R sell a third and lift the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell it all and lock in the 3R: Trims are thirds, and the last third is trailed.
wrong.Sell half, leave the stop alone: The hard rule is a third.
wrong.Hold all, nudge the stop up: The first third comes off at 3R.

questions.q: When do you take the first trim?
choices: At the open, 158.00
At the close
When it falls back to 157.32
Wait for 5R
questions.story: Your 3R level is 157.32. The next morning the Oops opens at 158.00.
questions.why: At the open, 158.00. If a day opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Open past the level, take the trim at the open.

wrong.At the close: The rule is to take it at the open.
wrong.When it falls back to 157.32: You may never get that price back.
wrong.Wait for 5R: The first third comes off at 3R. The open is past it.

questions.q: Your move on day 10?
choices: Sell it and free the money
Hold on and wait for 5R
Add on a break of the range
Widen the stop for more room
questions.story: It is day 10. The Oops has chopped sideways at +0.5R. The stop has not been touched.
questions.answer: Sell it and free the money
questions.why: Sell it. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and under 1R: sell and use the money elsewhere.

wrong.Hold on and wait for 5R: A trade under 1R after 10 days is sold.

questions.q: Williams' exit, the first profitable open, is our exit.
questions.why: False. Williams' bailout sells at the first profitable open. Ours is a third at 3R, a third at 5R and a trail.
questions.lesson_line: Williams' exit is his. Ours is thirds and a trail.

questions.q: How do you play it?
choices: Take it only if it is an A+
Full size, the same as Green
Pass, only Green allows it
Short the market index instead
questions.story: A clean Oops reclaims the prior close, but the market reading is Orange.
questions.answer: Take it only if it is an A+
questions.why: Take it only as an A+. In an Orange market only A+ setups. Green is full risk, Yellow smaller and fewer.
questions.lesson_line: Orange market, A+ only. Yellow, smaller. Green, full.

wrong.Pass, only Green allows it: Orange allows an A+. Red is mostly cash.
wrong.Short the market index instead: Red is mostly cash and shorts. Orange still allows an A+ long.

questions.q: Which average is the default trail for a fast mover?
choices: The 10-day
The 50-day
The 200-day
The 5-day
questions.why: The 10-day. Sell on a close below it. Steadier names trail the 21-day.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 10-day. Steadier name, 21-day. Sell on a close below.

wrong.The 50-day: Too slow for the default trail.
wrong.The 200-day: That is the long-term line, far too slow for a trail.
wrong.The 5-day: The defaults are the 10-day and the 21-day.

questions.q: In our data the Oops-day low broke within 20 sessions on about three Oops days in four.
questions.why: True. The low broke within 20 sessions on 75% of all Oops days. That is why the stop is the plan and the trims matter.
questions.lesson_line: The low usually breaks later. Take the thirds as they come.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Mostly cash; no Oops longs
Take it at full size
Take it at half size
Take it with a tighter stop
questions.story: A clean Oops reclaims the prior close, but the market reading is Red.
questions.why: Mostly cash. In a Red market it is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Red market: cash first. The Oops waits.

wrong.Take it at half size: In Red the answer is mostly cash.
wrong.Take it with a tighter stop: A tighter stop does not fix the market.

questions.q: How do you treat the new high?
choices: A new trade needs a new trigger
Buy it back now, you were right
Blame the stop and widen it
Skip it for good, it failed
questions.story: You bought at 176.35 with the stop at 174.16. The next day it fell through the stop. Four weeks later the stock makes a new high.
questions.answer: A new trade needs a new trigger
questions.why: A new trade needs a new trigger. The stop did its job. The second chance on V was a new trigger, not a hold.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is the plan working. Re-enter only on a new trigger.

wrong.Buy it back now, you were right: Buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade.
wrong.Skip it for good, it failed: The stock is fine to trade again on a new trigger.

questions.q: The app's 2R and 3R targets are our Oops plan.
questions.why: False. Treating the app's 2R and 3R targets as the plan is a named mistake. The house plan is 3R and 5R thirds.
questions.lesson_line: The plan is thirds at 3R and 5R, not the app targets.

questions.q: An Oops is better above a rising 200-day than a falling one.
questions.why: True. Prefer a rising 200-day. Under the 200-day is no trade at all.
questions.lesson_line: A rising 200-day under the stock is the better floor.

questions.q: Oops or 2B?
choices: An Oops, judged on yesterday's low
A 2B, it reclaimed the same day
A Red to Green
questions.story: Yesterday: low 49.40, close 50.00. Today opens at 49.70, trades under 49.40 and closes at 50.30. There is no older swing low nearby.
questions.answer: An Oops, judged on yesterday's low
questions.why: An Oops. It broke yesterday's low and reclaimed the prior close the same day. A 2B breaks an older swing low.
questions.lesson_line: Count the age of the broken low. Yesterday's low is an Oops.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the same day: A 2B breaks a swing low, not yesterday's low.
wrong.A Red to Green: A Red to Green is only the trade back through the prior close. This broke the prior low first.

questions.q: Is it an Oops?
choices: No, it is a 2B on an older low
Yes, it reclaimed a close
Yes, it is a Super Oops
questions.story: On Monday the stock breaks a swing low from twelve sessions ago. It closes back above that low on Tuesday.
questions.answer: No, it is a 2B on an older low
questions.why: No. It broke an older swing low and took until Tuesday to close back above it. A 2B may take up to 3 sessions; an Oops is one candle.
questions.lesson_line: One candle is an Oops. An older low and a day or two is a 2B.

wrong.Yes, it reclaimed a close: An Oops is judged on one candle and yesterday's low.
wrong.Yes, it is a Super Oops: A Super Oops is an Oops that closes over the prior high.

questions.q: Oops or U&R?
choices: A U&R, the level is an average
An Oops, it reclaimed fast
A Kicker
questions.story: The stock dips under its rising 50-day average and closes back above it the next day. It never traded under the prior day's low on the reclaim day.
questions.answer: A U&R, the level is an average
questions.why: A U&R. The level is a rising average, not yesterday's low, and a U&R's reclaim may take up to 3 sessions. An Oops is one candle.
questions.lesson_line: A bigger level and a few days: U&R. Yesterday's low in one day: Oops.

wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed fast: An Oops needs a trade under the prior day's low in one candle.
wrong.A Kicker: A Kicker gaps up. This is a dip under an average.

questions.q: Oops or Kicker?
choices: A Kicker, it gapped up
An Oops, it closed over the high
A Super Oops
questions.story: Yesterday was a red day. Today the stock gaps up over its close and closes above that day's high.
questions.why: A Kicker. A Kicker gaps up over a red day's close and is bought through the red day's high. An Oops opens down under the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: The gap direction decides it. Up is a Kicker. Down is an Oops.

wrong.An Oops, it closed over the high: An Oops opens down under the prior close. This gapped up.
wrong.A Super Oops: A Super Oops is still an Oops, which opens under the prior close.

questions.q: Oops or Red to Green?
choices: A Red to Green, not an Oops
An Oops, it closed over the close
A 2B
questions.story: The stock opens under the prior close and closes over it. Its low stays 0.48% above the prior day's low.
questions.answer: A Red to Green, not an Oops
questions.why: A Red to Green. The day's low held above the prior low, so it never undercut yesterday's low. That was GOOGL on 2026-02-27.
questions.lesson_line: Check if it traded under yesterday's low first. If not, it is a Red to Green.

wrong.An Oops, it closed over the close: An Oops needs a trade under the prior low first.
wrong.A 2B: A 2B breaks a swing low. This broke nothing.

questions.q: Oops or Go Signal?
choices: A Go Signal, it fires on the hourly
An Oops, it undercut a range
A Kicker
questions.story: After a catalyst gap, a stock digests in an hourly flag. It undercuts a slight range and goes red to green in the first hour.
questions.answer: A Go Signal, it fires on the hourly
questions.why: A Go Signal. A Go Signal is an hourly flag that goes red to green in the first hour. The Oops is the daily candle's reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: The chart that fires it decides. Daily candle is the Oops. Hourly flag is the Go Signal.

wrong.An Oops, it undercut a range: The Oops is read on the daily candle, not an hourly flag.
wrong.A Kicker: A Kicker is a daily gap up over a red day.

questions.q: Is it an Oops?
choices: No, it is a delayed reaction
Yes, it passes all three tests
Yes, but only half size
questions.story: The prior day fell from 126.58 to 118.08 on news. Today the stock opens under that close, undercuts the low by 0.10% and closes just over the prior close.
questions.answer: No, it is a delayed reaction
questions.why: No. The prior day fell 6.71%, a news day. The day after a news day is a delayed-reaction setup, not an Oops. That was PANW on 2023-08-03.
questions.lesson_line: A reversal after a news bar is not an Oops.

wrong.Yes, it passes all three tests: The three tests pass, but the prior day was a news bar. That is not an orderly pullback.
wrong.Yes, but only half size: Size does not fix a news-day setup.

questions.q: Which rule fails?
choices: No pullback: it sits at the highs
The undercut is missing
The close is under the prior close
The stop is over 3%
questions.story: The stock opens under the prior close, undercuts the prior low and closes over the prior close. The prior close was 0.6% under the 20-day high.
questions.answer: No pullback: it sits at the highs
questions.why: No pullback. The prior close was only 0.6% under the 20-day high, a dip at the highs with nothing to reverse from. That was HD on 2025-09-15.
questions.lesson_line: A dip at the highs is not a pullback.

wrong.The undercut is missing: The stock did undercut the prior low.
wrong.The close is under the prior close: It closed over the prior close.
wrong.The stop is over 3%: The failing rule is the pullback, not the stop.

questions.q: Why do the rules skip it?
choices: It is under the 200-day
The undercut was too deep
It closed too strong
The pullback was too long
questions.story: A textbook Oops day. The Oops-day close and the prior close are both 12% under the 200-day average.
questions.why: It is under the 200-day. Both closes were about 12% below it. No longs below the 200-day. That was BABA on 2016-02-24.
questions.lesson_line: An Oops shape under the 200-day is watch only.

wrong.The undercut was too deep: The undercut was not the problem.

questions.q: Is it a Williams Oops?
choices: No, it opened above the prior low
Yes, it opened under the close
Yes, it undercut the low
questions.story: Yesterday: high 50.60, low 49.40, close 50.00. Today: open 49.70, low 49.10, close 50.30.
questions.answer: No, it opened above the prior low
questions.why: No. A Williams Oops opens under the prior low. This opened at 49.70, over the prior low of 49.40. It is still the main Oops.
questions.lesson_line: Williams opens under the prior low. The main Oops opens under the close.

wrong.Yes, it opened under the close: That is the main Oops. Williams' version opens under the prior low.
wrong.Yes, it undercut the low: The undercut is part of every Oops. Williams also opens under the low.

questions.q: What did the Super close buy you?
choices: Nothing; it grades the setup
A guaranteed trend
A wider stop
A bigger size
questions.story: A Super Oops closes at 167.00 over the 166.53 prior high. You bought at 157.19 with the stop at 155.55. The next day opens at 165.36 and falls to 151.52.
questions.why: Nothing. A Super close is a grade mark, not a guarantee. AMAT closed over the prior high on 2022-01-14 and fell through its stop.
questions.lesson_line: A Super close grades the setup. It does not guarantee it.

wrong.A wider stop: The stop is the Oops-day low, whatever the close.

questions.q: What did the daily chart miss?
choices: The market was not Green
The pullback was too shallow
The close was too weak
The stop was too wide
questions.story: A Williams open after a red day, an 8.7% pullback to the 21-day. You bought at 74.97 with the stop at 73.73. The next day it is stopped as the index makes a lower low.
questions.why: The market was not Green. UBER reclaimed on 2025-03-07 and was stopped the next day as SPY made a lower low.
questions.lesson_line: The chart looks fine. The reading is the filter.

wrong.The pullback was too shallow: An 8.7% pullback is well inside the 3% to 12% range.

questions.q: Your move after the stop-out?
choices: Take the loss; the setup was right
Move the stop lower next time
Rewrite the rules after one stop-out
Buy it right back at the open
questions.story: A clean Oops with a red prior day, a pullback to the 21-day and a strong close. Two days later it trades under the Oops-day low and you are stopped out.
questions.answer: Take the loss; the setup was right
questions.why: Take the planned loss. A good example can have a horrible result. WFRD and SEI are the named cases. Do not expect every Oops to work.
questions.lesson_line: A good setup can lose. The loss was planned.

wrong.Move the stop lower next time: A stop never moves down or wider.
wrong.Rewrite the rules after one stop-out: One loss on a good setup is part of the system.
wrong.Buy it right back at the open: Buy again only on a new trigger.

questions.q: What went wrong?
choices: Nothing; a Super close is no guarantee
The stop was too tight
You should have bought the close
The prior day was not red
questions.story: A Super Oops closes over the prior high with a 1.52% stop. The next day it opens a little lower and sells through the stop.
questions.answer: Nothing; a Super close is no guarantee
questions.why: Nothing went wrong with the rules. CRM was a Super Oops on 2023-06-20 and sold through the stop the next day. The Super close is a grade mark.
questions.lesson_line: A clean Oops can still fail. The stop is the plan.

wrong.The stop was too tight: The stop sits under the Oops-day low, not where the day felt safe.
wrong.You should have bought the close: The close is not the entry.
wrong.The prior day was not red: A red prior day is preferred, not required.

questions.q: What did the stop do?
choices: Its job: a small planned loss
Cost you the trade; it needed room
Nothing; the close was the exit
questions.story: You bought at 176.35 with the stop at 174.16. The next day it opens at 176.24 and falls to 173.16 without trading above your entry.
questions.answer: Its job: a small planned loss
questions.why: Its job. V never traded above the entry, and the stop took the loss the next day. The second chance later was a new trigger.
questions.lesson_line: A loss at plan is the system working.

wrong.Cost you the trade; it needed room: Room is how a small loss becomes a big one.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, yesterday's close. Tomorrow it undercuts the low and reclaims the close. Take it or pass?
choices: Take it; a leader onto two averages
Pass; there is no pullback
Pass; a news bar came first
questions.answer: Take it; a leader onto two averages
questions.why: Take it. A clean leader drifted three weeks onto its converging 21-day and 50-day. The undercut tagged both and it closed over the prior high.
questions.lesson_line: Judge the setup yesterday: orderly drift onto averages.

wrong.Pass; there is no pullback: It drifted 5.2% off its high, inside the 3% to 12% range.
wrong.Pass; a news bar came first: The drift was orderly. No news bar.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, yesterday's close. Tomorrow it undercuts the low and reclaims the close. Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; it sits at the highs, no pullback
Take it; the reclaim is the trigger
Take it; the 200-day is rising
questions.answer: Pass; it sits at the highs, no pullback
questions.why: Pass. The prior close was only 0.6% under the 20-day high, a dip at the highs. There is nothing to reverse from.
questions.lesson_line: No pullback, no Oops. A dip at the highs is not it.

wrong.Take it; the reclaim is the trigger: The reclaim is a trigger only after a real pullback.
wrong.Take it; the 200-day is rising: A rising 200-day is a plus, not a substitute for the pullback.

questions.q: Every Oops is a red to green, and every red to green is an Oops.
questions.why: False. Every Oops is a red to green, but not the reverse. An Oops must first trade under the prior low.
questions.lesson_line: Oops is the narrower one. It needs the undercut first.

questions.q: The best Oops days are market-wide gap downs that reverse, when leaders print Oops together.
questions.why: True. When the whole market gaps down and reverses, the leaders print Oops together. Those are the best days for the setup.
questions.lesson_line: A whole-market gap down that reverses is the best Oops day.
